title: Delamination Front Propagation
introduction: When thermally accumulated strain energy at a film interface exceeds the fracture toughness of that interface, a delamination crack initiates and a delamination front advances across the bonded area. This energy-balance governed process separates thin-film device layers from their substrate, exposing buried interfaces and disrupting the electrical continuity and protective function of the multi-layer stack. In CdTe solar cells, the delamination front propagates along the weak CdS/TCO buried interface when the strain energy release rate threshold is met under thermal quench conditions.
reasoning: The 011-ACS study explicitly frames delamination as crack growth governed by an energy balance (SERR vs. fracture toughness) and measures delamination front growth rate, establishing this as a distinct mechanism downstream of thermal strain buildup.

key_findings.claim: Delamination initiates when the strain energy release rate at the interface exceeds the interface fracture toughness
key_findings.detail: For delamination to occur at any given interface, the energy released during crack advance must be larger than the fracture toughness of that interface. [^acs011c] This energy balance criterion governs whether stored thermal mismatch strain energy is sufficient to propagate the delamination crack front across the bonded film area.

source_locations.quote: For delamination to occur at a given interface, the energy released during delamination must be larger than the interface fracture toughness

key_findings.claim: Delamination front growth rate increases sharply once the strain energy threshold is crossed
key_findings.detail: Once the strain energy release rate exceeds the interface fracture toughness, the growth rate of the delamination front accelerates at a far higher rate than during the energy buildup phase. [^acs011d] This non-linear response means small additional increases in quench depth or cycling frequency can produce dramatically faster delamination under field conditions.
